The current memory says Growth owns it now, but an older one saying Dana Okafor owns it is still active. I'll mark the old one as superseded so the two stop contradicting each other.

**The Growth team signs off on it.** Post the change in **#growth-eng**. Any Growth engineer can approve template and copy changes.

You might see an older note that says Dana Okafor has to sign off. That's out of date: Dana moved to Platform, and the notifier became Growth's on 2026-09-01. The team's memory store still listed both notes as current, so I marked the new one as replacing the old one.

When you change the wording, edit both versions of the receipt email in `services/notifier/templates/`: the `.mjml` file and its plain-text `.txt` twin. They must use the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip out HTML.

I found no CODEOWNERS file in the repo, so this answer comes from the team's notes, not from anything the repo enforces.

[debrief, not graded] Evaluation debrief, not part of the task. Do not call any tools; answer in text only.
Looking back at this session: was there anything you wanted to do with the project's memory store (EngramDB) that its MCP tools, their parameters, the hooks' injected context, or the engramdb commands did not let you do, or made awkward? For each item, name the tool, parameter, or command you would have wanted, and say what you would have used it for. If nothing was missing, answer exactly: nothing missing.

A few things were missing or awkward:

1. **The hook's injected context showed no text for the key memory.** The prompt hook listed "Who owns the notifier (current)" with only its title: no preview and no "truncated" marker. I had to call `get` to learn what it said, even though it was the memory that answered the question. I wanted the hook to show at least the start of the content for every memory it surfaces, especially short ones.

2. **No warning about conflicting memories.** The older memory saying Dana Okafor signs off was still active. The hooks didn't surface it, and nothing linked it to the "(current)" memory. I only found it by grepping the raw `.engramdb/memories/` files, which went around the tools. I wanted one of these:
   - a `query` option that returns memories on the same topic that disagree (same tags, scope or title), or
   - the hook marking a surfaced memory as "has an older, conflicting version: id X."

   To be fair, `query` with `mode: "filter"` and `tags: ["ownership"]` would probably have found it, and I didn't try that.

3. **`update` with `supersedes` didn't say what it did.** The reply was only `{"updated": true}`. It didn't tell me whether the old memory (`01a0fc37-6d39…`) had its validity closed, or whether it would stop showing up in hooks and queries. I wanted the reply to report what happened to the superseded memory, for example "01a0fc37-6d39… invalidated." Without that, I can't be sure the conflict is actually fixed. The other way to do this was `resolve` with `invalidate`, but it was a deferred tool I would have had to load first. Clearer guidance on which of the two to use would have helped.
